## Why does a biologist need code?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**By hand**

- 1 FASTA file → OK
- 500 FASTA files → a week of copy & paste
- "Which version of the table did I use?" 🤯
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**With code**

- 500 files → one script, a few seconds
- Same result every time
- Full history of every change
:::
::::

::: notes
Keep it short. The goal is motivation, not a lecture.
:::

## Interview your partner 🎤

Breakout rooms · 2 people · **5 minutes**

1. What's your name and what do you study?
2. Your favourite organism / field of biology?
3. One thing you are afraid of in this course?
4. One thing you would like to be able to do after this course?

. . .

Back in the main room: introduce **your partner** in one sentence.

::: notes
30–45 min. Paste the 4 questions in the chat BEFORE opening the rooms (slides are not visible in breakout rooms).
Random pairs. With a big group: introductions in the chat instead of speaking, then read a few aloud.
:::

# How this course works

## What we will learn

| Weeks | Topic |
|---|---|
| 1 | **Git** & GitHub — from day one |
| 2 | Terminal & Bash |
| 3–7 | Python basics |
| 8 | Git in teams |
| 9–11 | Python + Bash together, mini-project |
| 12–13 | R basics |
| 14 | Oral exams — talking about your project 💬 |

::: notes
45–65 min: course rules (incl. short Q&A at the end).
:::

## How a typical class looks

| Time | What happens |
|---|---|
| 10 min | Warm-up task |
| 15 min | Something new (short!) |
| 10 min | Live coding — you tell me in the chat what to type |
| 35 min | **You** code in pairs (breakout rooms) |
| 10 min | Discussion + `git commit` + `git push` |

. . .

**Less listening, more coding.**

## Rules of our online room

- 🎥 Camera on during pair work, if you can
- 👥 Pairs: one **shares the screen**, the other guides — switch every 10 min
- ✅ Reaction = *"it works"* · ✋ Raise hand = *"I need help"*
- ⏱️ Stuck for **more than 5 minutes**? Write in the chat
- ❌ Errors are normal — reading them is a skill we will learn
- 💾 Every class ends with a **commit**

::: notes
Stress the 5-minute rule: online, beginners get stuck silently.
:::

## Assessment

| Component | When | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| 📝 Quizzes (7 short online quizzes) | every ~2 weeks | 15% |
| 👥 Pair assignment (Git teamwork) | week 8 | 25% |
| 🧬 Final project (individual) + oral exam | week 14 | 60% |

## Oral exam 💬

- **15 minutes** per person, in the last week of classes
- We talk about **your final project code**
- Goal: see what **you** have learned

. . .

> This is a **conversation, not an interrogation.** 🙂

. . .

No attendance tracking — but practice in class is where you learn.

::: notes
Oral exam questions ideas: walk me through your script; why did you use a dictionary here; what would you change; what was the hardest part.
Timing: week 14 has 160 min → only ~10 students in class time. Plan extra slots if the group is bigger.
:::

## AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude…)

✅ **OK**

- Explaining an error message
- Explaining what a piece of code does

❌ **Not OK**

- Generating complete solutions to assignments
- Submitting code you cannot explain

. . .

> Rule of thumb: **if you can't explain it, don't submit it.**

# Getting ready for Block 2

## Create a GitHub account 🐙

Breakout rooms · pairs · help each other

1. Go to **github.com** → *Sign up*
2. Use an e-mail you check regularly
3. Choose a **professional** username (e.g. `firstname-lastname`)
4. Confirm your e-mail
5. Post your username in the chat 📝

::: notes
65–80 min. Paste the steps in the chat before opening rooms. Collect usernames from the chat.
:::

## If you have time left ⏳

Open a terminal and type:

```bash
git --version
```

- **Windows:** install *Git for Windows* → use **Git Bash**
- **macOS:** open *Terminal* (it may ask to install developer tools — say yes)
- **Linux:** usually already installed

React with ✅ when you see a version number.
